newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-COLLETER AIMS TO UPSET PSG TITLE CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLLETER AIMS TO UPSET PSG TITLE CHALLENGE.

text.p: Bordeaux captain Patrick Colleter, who helped Paris Saint-Germain win European honours in May, is now aiming to damage their French league title hopes on Saturday.

The defender, who moved southwest after the Cup Winners' Cup victory, feared a long suspension might keep him out of the clash with his ex-team mates after he elbowed Nantes striker Jocelyn Gourvennec in the face a month ago.
"If I'd been suspended for this match, I think I would have suffered a lot," said Colleter, who in the end was only banned for one game, missing the midweek 4-3 victory at Lens.
"PSG is a heavy machine. They've only lost once this season and (Saturday's match) is not going to be run of the mill."
Bordeaux rested several first choice players for the trip to Lens, including six-goal Jean-Pierre Papin, who will lead the attack with Argentine Claudio Biaggio or Senegal's Kaba Diawara.
Coach Rolland Courbis, referring to the reserves, said: "These youngsters allowed some players to take a breather.
"These four or five youngsters had their minds on that (Lens) match, not on the visit of Paris Saint-Germain on Saturday as the regular first team players might have.

Papin, Colleter and Biaggio are among a large number of new recruits at Bordeaux this season after the team that reached the UEFA Cup final last season was decimated by transfers, notably those of Zinedine Zidane and Christophe Dugarry to Italian clubs and Bixente Lizarazu to Athletic Bilbao.

Colleter and his fellow defenders can expect a tough time trying to contain a PSG attack that has been in fine form since the 4-0 home win over Galatasaray of Turkey last month that ensured they progressed to the Cup Winners' Cup quarter-finals.
PSG had just lost their unbeaten record against Rennes. They went on to win their next three league games, scoring seven goals and conceding one.

Panama's Julio Cesar Dely Valdes has scored five times in the four successive wins, taking his league tally to six goals, one less than Brazilian team mate Leonardo, the leaders' chief creative force.

The Parisians' defence, the best in the league, will also be put under severe strain by a Bordeaux side whose confidence has returned after a black October during which they lost sucessive home games to Strasbourg and relegation candidates Nancy.
